input.question: please explain how tax incentives, like the 35 million Man of Steel 2 will be getting for filming in Detroit, work.
input.ground_truth: That cash will likely be used to offset production costs, resulting in higher profits -- slightly higher, at least, but not much considering the scale of the money they are spending on the movie in the first place. The point of the tax credit is that it will make it easier for them to hire more people than their original budget allowed; ideally, the government would want them to spend that entire $35m in Detroit in order to boost the economy.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: please explain how tax incentives, like the 35 million Man of Steel 2 will be getting for filming in Detroit, work.

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a lemonade stand, and the city really wants you to set up your stand in their neighborhood instead of somewhere else. So, the city gives you some free cookies and a few extra lemons to help you make more lemonade if you set up your stand there.

That’s kind of how tax incentives work for movies. The city or state gives the movie people some money back (or helps them save money) if they come and film in that place. For “Man of Steel 2,” the city of Detroit is giving them some money (like those free lemons and cookies) to help them make their movie there. This helps the city because it brings jobs and excitement, and it helps the movie people because they get to save money or get extra help.
